concerns.text: T009–T011 write four separate files (paired_t_test.json, quadratic_fit.json, sensitivity_analysis.json, entropy_error_corr.json), but the active schema requires ONE object with t_test_result, quadratic_coefficients, peak_density, sensitivity_slopes, entropy_error_correlation, and analysis_timestamp all as required fields. No individual file can validate, so T013's verification ('validates every JSON in data/results/ … against the schemas') is unexecutable as written. Either write a single consolidated statistical_result.json or restructure the schema.

T014 requires re-running `--config configs/quickstart.yaml` from a clean checkout and confirming 'all artifacts listed in docs/results.md regenerate', but quickstart.yaml is introduced in T001 only as a thin init config ('prints Pipeline initialized'). It is unspecified whether quickstart.yaml triggers the full 25+ run suite; if not, the verification cannot confirm regeneration of results.md artifacts. State which config regenerates the full suite (and its wall-clock feasibility) or scope the re-run to the thin path.

T002 defines `load_gsm8k(split, streaming=True)` but the verification calls `load_gsm8k('test')` with no streaming argument and applies `len(d)`. If the default return is an IterableDataset, `len()` raises TypeError. Specify that the loader returns the materialized fixed sample (list/Dataset) so `len(d) == 500` is checkable, and make the signature/verification consistent.

T007's adaptive and control runs give no timeout/checkpoint procedure; only T005 implements the epoch-start wall-clock check. The T007 verification ('10 schema-valid JSON files') is executable, but a hung adaptive run would never produce a file — add the same timeout enforcement statement to T007 so its verification is reachable under failure conditions.

T011 sweeps ±0.05/±0.1 around the T010 peak with seed 42 only; if the clamped peak lands on a grid value (e.g., 0.5), some offsets duplicate T005 runs — note whether existing rho0.5_seed42.json may be reused or must be re-run, so the implementer knows the expected file set.
